newsitem.title: UK: Safeway shares relieved at sales gain.
newsitem.headline: Safeway shares relieved at sales gain.

text.p: British supermarkets group Safeway Plc turned in annual profits broadly as expected on Wednesday and gave a boost to its shares with better than expected news on sales.
"There is a relief factor in the share price gain, the sales were better than a lot of people were expecting," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Safeway also said it planned to create 8,000 jobs over the next two years, including the addition of 1,600 customer service and support staff this year with investment of 10 million pounds ($16.3 million).
The company, known for its technological innovations, said that sales from existing stores were currently showing gains of 4.6 percent compared to a 4.7 percent rise in the year to March 29.
But prices were down 0.9 percent currently, however, after it saw price inflation of two percent last year.
It said pretax profits rose seven percent to 430.1 million pounds and paid out a total dividend of 14.10 pence per share, up from 12.75 pence previously.
Shares shot up to be 18 pence higher at 349 pence by 1029 GMT, just off a high of 351 pence, as the market welcomed the better than expected sales news.
There had been concerns that Safeway would be squeezed as J. Sainsbury reported sales from existing stores inching up to 4.2 percent gains at annual results last week.

Safeway still lags behind market leader Tesco'S six percent like-for-like sales growth but some analysts had feared that sales might have dropped off, with growth forecast nearer two to three percent.
Safeway also said gross margin was currently slightly down on the previous year, continuing the trend of the second half of last year and again better than analysts had feared.
"The comment on gross margins was taken more positively," another analyst said.
Safeway finance director Simon Laffin said the group was trying to improve gross margin but stressed the need to stay competitive.
Safeway has "a lot of initiatives which do try to raise the gross margin...nevertheless, we are absolutely firm that we will remain competitive," Laffin told Reuters.
He said Safeway had been "very successful" in targeting family shoppers and persuading people to make the group its first choice for main shopping trips.

"The proportion of our target family shoppers who spend more than 40 pounds per visit -- which is a basic benchmark of doing their main shop -- that's risen from 17 to 18 percent," Laffin said, making up a quarter of Safeway's consumers.
"We are very precisely targetting...young families and we are proving successful at getting them," he added.
Safeway's award-winning advertising campaign features two children, Harry and Molly, with adult voiceovers which allow them to appear wiser than their years.

It also has 50 stores with creches and intends to roll this out to 100 while it is already the largest private sector employer of nursery nurses, Laffin said. Chief executive Colin Smith said in the results statement that the "key performance objective this year is to achieve higher volume sales growth," adding that Safeway would do this through strengthening its offer to family shoppers, improving service and addressing standards of product availability.
Laffin said that gearing, which went to 33 percent after last year's share buyback, was within range which balanced an efficient capital structure with giving opportunities to invest.
"I don't think (a buyback) is something that's immediately on the agenda, but we will retain the ablility to do it if circumstances change," he said.
Laffin said Safeway felt there was still opportunity to invest in the UK, with possibilities mainly in organic growth.

Safeway has a target for efficiency savings of 0.2 percent of sales yearly, which Laffin said it would aim for again during the current year, giving it "an ability to at least partially offset gross margin investment."
"We won't be changing our year profit forecasts much, the short-term news is good but I don't think six weeks is long enough," the sector analyst said.
($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
